cases.description: Microsoft's documented worked example for the legacy (pre-2010) name: cumulative beta distribution at x=2, alpha=8, beta=10 on [1,3]
cases.expected_note: Microsoft's page publishes this example's result as 0.6854706, the same figure as the modern BETA.DIST page. Independently derived from the regularized incomplete beta function: scipy.special.betainc(8,10,(2-1)/(3-1)) = betainc(8,10,0.5) = 0.6854705810546875 -> 0.6854706 at 7 dp. BETADIST has no `cumulative` argument -- it is always the CDF

cases.description: The same distribution on the default interval, with A and B omitted
cases.expected_note: Excel documents "If you omit values for A and B, BETADIST uses the standard cumulative beta distribution, so that A = 0 and B = 1", and x=2 on [1,3] rescales to exactly 0.5 on [0,1], so the result must be identical to the documented example
Excel documents: "If alpha <= 0 or beta <= 0, BETADIST returns the #NUM! error value."

cases.description: An x value below the lower bound A
cases.expected_note: Excel documents: "If x < A, x > B, or A = B, BETADIST returns the #NUM! error value." Here x = 0 is below A = 1
Excel documents the same rule for the degenerate case A = B, where the rescaling (x-A)/(B-A) would divide by zero -- note the documented error is #NUM!, not #DIV/0!
Excel documents: "If any argument is nonnumeric, BETADIST returns the #VALUE! error value."
